questions.title: Barbie — Age, Unit Conversions, a House Plan and Box Surface Area

subQuestions.questionText: Barbie was introduced on 9 March 1959 by Mattel. Determine how old Barbie is currently (as at 2022, ignoring months and days).
subQuestions.memoText:
2022 − 1959 = 63 years old

Mark 1: 2022 − 1959
Mark 2: 63 years

subQuestions.questionText: Barbie is 12 inches (30,5 cm) tall. Determine how many centimetres there are in an inch by completing the calculation with the correct operation (+, −, ×, ÷), rounding to two decimal places: 30,5 cm ___ 12 inches = ______ cm/inch.
subQuestions.memoText:
30,5 cm ÷ 12 inches = 2,54 cm/inch

Mark 1: choosing ÷
Mark 2: 2,54 cm/inch

subQuestions.questionText: More than 151 000 000 minutes of content has been watched on the Barbie YouTube channel. Write the number of minutes in words without using number values.
subQuestions.memoText:
One hundred and fifty-one million

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: 151 000 000 minutes is equivalent to 41 944,44 hours. Write this in hours and minutes, rounded to the nearest minute.
subQuestions.memoText:
0,44 hours × 60 = 26,4 minutes ≈ 26 minutes
41 944 hours and 26 minutes (accept 41 944 hours and 27 minutes)

Mark 1: converting the decimal part of the hour to minutes
Mark 2: 41 944 hours and 26 minutes

subQuestions.questionText: A Barbie house design plan is shown with outer dimensions: length 94 cm, height 123,4 cm, width 69 cm. Determine how many floors are found in this Barbie house.
subQuestions.memoText:
3 floors

[Award 2 marks for reading the design plan correctly]

subQuestions.questionText: The outer length of the Barbie house is 94 cm, and the outer width of each frame panel is 5 cm. Calculate the inner length of this Barbie house.
subQuestions.memoText:
Inner length = 94 cm − (2 × 5 cm) = 94 − 10 = 84 cm

Mark 1: subtracting 2 × 5 cm
Mark 2: answer 84 cm

subQuestions.questionText: A Barbie Princess doll is sold for R154,99 at Checkers. Round off R154,99 to the nearest R10.
subQuestions.memoText:
R154,99 ≈ R150

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Using your answer in Question 1.5.1 (R150), calculate in dollars the cost of the doll if R1 is equal to $0,066.
The height of the doll's box is 320 mm. Convert 320 mm to cm by completing the calculation: 320 mm ___ = ______ cm.
subQuestions.memoText:
320 mm ÷ 10 = 32 cm

Mark 1: ÷ 10
Mark 2: answer 32 cm

subQuestions.questionText: The total surface area for the box can be calculated using which formula?
subQuestions.memoText:
B — 2(L × B) + 2(L × H) + 2(B × H)

[Award 2 marks for identifying option B]

subQuestions.questionText: The total surface area of the box is 1 258 cm². 7% of the box is made of plastic to display the doll. Calculate the total area covered by the plastic.
subQuestions.memoText:
Plastic area = 7% × 1 258 = 0,07 × 1 258 = 88,06 cm² (accept 88 cm²)

Mark 1: 7% of 1 258
Mark 2: answer 88,06 cm²

subQuestions.questionText: Convert 1 258 cm² to mm².
The correct unit of measurement for volume is:
subQuestions.memoText:
C — cm³

[Award 2 marks for identifying option C]

subQuestions.questionText: A pattern for a Barbie apron skirt is shown, with an overall measurement of 6,3 cm and an inner (skirt) measurement of 5 cm. Calculate the width (W) of the lace border.
subQuestions.memoText:
W = 6,3 cm − 5 cm = 1,3 cm
(OR from the marked pieces: 4,8 cm − 3,5 cm = 1,3 cm)

Mark 1: subtracting the two measurements
Mark 2: answer 1,3 cm

subQuestions.questionText: There are 7 military Barbie careers: Army medic; Paratrooper; Air Force pilot; Air Force Thunderbirds pilot; Army officer; Marine Corps sergeant; Navy petty officer. If a child selects a Military Barbie at random, what is the probability that the child will select a pilot?
subQuestions.memoText:
B — 2/7 (there are two pilot careers: Air Force pilot and Air Force Thunderbirds pilot)

[Award 2 marks for identifying option B]

questions.title: Growing Food on Mars — Recipe Scaling, Scale, Speed, Temperature and Matching

subQuestions.questionText: The Nettle Soup recipe uses 1 tsp of olive oil. If 1 teaspoon (tsp) = 5 cm³, determine which teaspoon (A, B or C) shown must be used to measure the olive oil needed for this recipe.
subQuestions.memoText:
Teaspoon B (the one marked 5 cm³ / 5 mℓ).

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: The recipe serves 4 people and uses 50 mℓ of double cream. A space shuttle carries 7 astronauts to Mars. Determine how much double cream would be needed to adjust the menu for 7 people.
subQuestions.memoText:
= 50 mℓ ÷ 4 × 7 = 87,5 mℓ (accept 88 mℓ)

Mark 1: 50 ÷ 4
Mark 2: × 7 → 87,5 mℓ

subQuestions.questionText: The recipe has a prep time of 20 minutes and a cooking time of 30 minutes. If the ingredients are increased to accommodate 7 people, the prep and cooking time increases by 12%. Determine how long it would now take to prepare and cook the soup.
subQuestions.memoText:
Original time = 20 + 30 = 50 minutes
Increase = 12% × 50 = 0,12 × 50 = 6 minutes
New time = 50 + 6 = 56 minutes

Mark 1: 20 + 30 = 50 minutes
Mark 2: 12% of 50
Mark 3: 50 + 6 = 56 minutes

subQuestions.questionText: A diagram of a space shuttle has a scale of 1 : 550. If the length of the space shuttle in real life is 54 m, use the scale to determine the length on the diagram in cm. (Do not measure the diagram with a ruler.)
subQuestions.memoText:
54 m ÷ 550 = 0,098 m = 9,8 cm
(OR 5 400 cm ÷ 550 = 9,8 cm)

Mark 1: dividing by the scale (550)
Mark 2: 0,098 m
Mark 3: converting to 9,8 cm

subQuestions.questionText: A space shuttle travels the 300 million miles distance to Mars at a speed of 24 600 miles per hour. Calculate how long (in months) it would take a space shuttle to reach Mars. Assume there are 30 days in a month. Use: Time = Distance ÷ Speed.
If 1 mile = 1,609344 km, determine the speed of the space shuttle (24 600 miles per hour) in km/h.

On 20/02/2022 the temperature on Mars ranged from −4 °F (maximum) to −98 °F (minimum). John calculated the difference between the maximum and minimum temperature to be 52,2 °C, with the minimum temperature at that point being −72,2 °C. Show with calculations whether John's calculations were correct. Use: °F = 1,8 × °C + 32.
subQuestions.memoText:
Convert the maximum −4 °F to °C:
−4 = 1,8 °C + 32
−4 − 32 = 1,8 °C
−36 = 1,8 °C
°C = −36 ÷ 1,8 = −20 °C
Difference = maximum − minimum = −20 − (−72,2) = −20 + 72,2 = 52,2 °C
John is correct.

Mark 1: −4 − 32
Mark 2: ÷ 1,8
Mark 3: maximum = −20 °C
Mark 4: −20 − (−72,2) = 52,2 °C — John is correct

subQuestions.questionText: Mars is 142 million miles from the sun and 51 000 000 miles away from Earth. Calculate how far Earth is from the sun. (Assume the sun, Earth and Mars are aligned in order on a straight line.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Earth to sun = 142 000 000 − 51 000 000 = 91 000 000 miles (91 million miles)

Mark 1: subtraction
Mark 2: answer 91 000 000 miles

subQuestions.questionText:
Match the instructions in Column A (2.3.1 to 2.3.6) for building a simple bottle rocket with the diagrams in Column B (A to F):
2.3.1 Gather your materials (plastic bottle, paper cone, two cardboard triangles, three pencils, water, bicycle pump).
2.3.2 Make a rocket from a bottle — tape a paper cone to the top and triangle fins on the sides.
2.3.3 Build a rocket stand — tape pencils around the sides pointing down.
2.3.4 Put water in the bottle — fill it half full.
2.3.5 Cork the bottle — replace the cap with a cork.
2.3.6 Pump air into the bottle — use a bicycle pump with a needle through the cork.
subQuestions.memoText:
2.3.1 → C
2.3.2 → F
2.3.3 → E
2.3.4 → B
2.3.5 → A
2.3.6 → D

[Award 1 mark per correct match]

questions.title: Mohamed Salah — Soccer Field Measurements, Stadium Seating and Match Probability

subQuestions.questionText: A standard soccer field is 120 m long and 90 m wide. As part of his training, Salah runs the total perimeter of the soccer field 5 times. Determine, in kilometres, the total distance Salah runs during training.
subQuestions.memoText:
Perimeter = 2 × (120 + 90) = 2 × 210 = 420 m
Total distance = 420 × 5 = 2 100 m = 2,1 km

Mark 1: 120 + 90
Mark 2: × 2 → perimeter 420 m
Mark 3: × 5 → 2 100 m
Mark 4: converting to 2,1 km

subQuestions.questionText: The penalty area is 40,3 m wide, and on each side there is a 5,5 m distance from the goal post to the edge of the penalty box. Calculate the length of the penalty box marked A.

The centre circle (B) has a radius of 9,15 m. The field is 120 m by 90 m. Determine what percentage of the soccer field's area is taken up by the centre circle. Use: Area of circle = 3,142 × r²; Area of rectangle = L × W.
subQuestions.memoText:
Area of field = 120 × 90 = 10 800 m²
Area of centre circle = 3,142 × 9,15² = 3,142 × 83,7225 = 263,02 m² (accept 263)
Percentage = 263,02 ÷ 10 800 × 100 = 2,4%

Mark 1: area of the field
Mark 2: substituting into the circle formula
Mark 3: area of the circle ≈ 263 m²
Mark 4: ÷ 10 800 × 100 → 2,4%

subQuestions.label: 3.1.4 (i)
subQuestions.questionText: A player's water bottle has a diameter of 7 cm, and the water level (dotted line) is at a height of 28,575 cm. Calculate, in litres, the capacity of the water in the water bottle. Use: Volume of cylinder = 3,142 × radius² × height; 1 cm³ = 1 mℓ.
subQuestions.memoText:
Radius = 7 ÷ 2 = 3,5 cm
Volume = 3,142 × 3,5² × 28,575
= 3,142 × 12,25 × 28,575
= 1 099,84 cm³
= 1 099,84 mℓ
= 1,1 litres

Mark 1: radius = 3,5 cm
Mark 2: substituting into the formula
Mark 3: 1 099,84 cm³ = 1 099,84 mℓ
Mark 4: converting to 1,1 litres

subQuestions.label: 3.1.4 (ii)
subQuestions.questionText: If the total height of the bottle is 13% more than the given height (28,575 cm), calculate, to the nearest cm, the total height of the bottle.
subQuestions.memoText:
= 28,575 × 1,13 = 32,29 cm ≈ 32 cm

Mark 1: × 1,13 (adding 13%)
Mark 2: 32,29 cm
Mark 3: rounding to the nearest cm → 32 cm

subQuestions.questionText: A picture shows Mohamed Salah aiming for a goal, with an angle marked θ on a measuring instrument (protractor). Read off the size of the angle marked θ.
subQuestions.memoText:
θ = 35° (allow ±1°)

[Award 2 marks for a correct reading]

subQuestions.questionText: The full seating capacity at Anfield stadium is 53 394. 40% of the seats are in the Main Stand, 1/5 of the seats are in the Anfield Road Stand and 20% are in the Centenary Stand. Determine what percentage of seats are in the KOP Stand.
subQuestions.memoText:
Anfield Road Stand = 1/5 = 20%
KOP Stand = 100% − 40% − 20% − 20% = 20%

Mark 1: 1/5 = 20%
Mark 2: subtracting from 100%
Mark 3: answer 20%

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the total number of seats in the Anfield Road Stand (1/5 of the 53 394 seats).
Tickets for the Anfield stadium cost £49 excluding 15% VAT. Calculate, including VAT, the income from ticket sales if the stadium is full to capacity (53 394 seats).

When Liverpool play at home the team has a 1/2 chance of winning, a 1/10 chance of drawing and a 2/5 chance of losing. When they play away they have a 4/10 chance of winning and an equal chance of drawing or losing. On the tree diagram, x is the away probability of a draw (and of a loss). Write down the value of x.
subQuestions.memoText:
Away: P(win) = 4/10, so P(draw) + P(lose) = 1 − 4/10 = 6/10
Split equally: x = 6/10 ÷ 2 = 3/10

Mark 1: 1 − 4/10
Mark 2: x = 3/10

subQuestions.questionText: Determine the probability (y) that Salah will draw a home game, given that P(HD) = P(H) × P(D), where P(H) = 1/2 (playing at home) and P(D) = 1/10 (drawing when at home).
Determine the probability that the team will win, regardless of playing at home or away. (P(home) = P(away) = 1/2; P(win | home) = 1/2; P(win | away) = 4/10.)

questions.title: Bathu Sneakers — Box Volume, Packing, Cardboard Cost and a Delivery Route

subQuestions.questionText: A pair of Bathu sneakers costs R1 200 and delivery charges cost R300 per order. Calculate the total cost for 2 pairs of sneakers delivered together in one order.
A Bathu shoe box has dimensions 26 cm (L) by 34,5 cm (B) by 19 cm (H). Determine the volume of the shoe box. Use: Volume of rectangular prism = L × B × H.
subQuestions.memoText:
V = 26 × 34,5 × 19 = 17 043 cm³

Mark 1: substituting the three dimensions
Mark 2: correct multiplication
Mark 3: answer 17 043 cm³

subQuestions.questionText: Multiple shoe boxes (26 cm × 34,5 cm × 19 cm) are packed into a transport box measuring 70 cm long, 51 cm wide and 15 inches high. Show, with calculations, if 4 boxes of sneakers will fit into this transport box. (1 inch = 2,54 cm.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Along the length: 70 ÷ 34,5 = 2,028 → 2 shoe boxes
Along the width: 51 ÷ 26 = 1,96 → 1 shoe box
Height of transport box: 15 × 2,54 = 38,1 cm; 38,1 ÷ 19 = 2,005 → 2 shoe boxes
Total = 2 × 1 × 2 = 4 shoe boxes
Yes, 4 boxes of sneakers will fit.

Mark 1: 70 ÷ 34,5 → 2
Mark 2: 51 ÷ 26 → 1
Mark 3: 15 × 2,54 = 38,1 cm
Mark 4: 38,1 ÷ 19 → 2
Mark 5: 2 × 1 × 2
Mark 6: = 4 boxes — they fit

subQuestions.questionText: The cost of the cardboard to make the boxes is 0,502 cents/cm². The larger (male) box uses 4 093 cm² of cardboard and the smaller (female) box uses 3 034 cm². Calculate the percentage saving Bathu Sneakers will make if the smaller box is used compared to the normal larger box.
subQuestions.memoText:
Large box: 4 093 × 0,502 = 2 054,686 cents = R20,54686
Small box: 3 034 × 0,502 = 1 523,068 cents = R15,23068
Saving = R20,54686 − R15,23068 = R5,31618 ≈ R5,32
Percentage saving = 5,32 ÷ 20,54686 × 100 = 25,89%

Mark 1: large box cost (4 093 × 0,502)
Mark 2: R20,55
Mark 3: small box cost (3 034 × 0,502)
Mark 4: R15,23
Mark 5: saving R5,32
Mark 6: ÷ large cost × 100 → 25,89%

subQuestions.label: 4.2.4 (i)
subQuestions.questionText: Sneakers are transported by truck to the Kimberley store. Using the map, underline the correct province: Upington lies in the Northern / Western / Eastern Cape.
subQuestions.memoText:
Northern Cape

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.label: 4.2.4 (ii)
subQuestions.questionText: In which general direction does Kimberley lie from Johannesburg?
subQuestions.memoText:
South-west

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.label: 4.2.4 (iii)
subQuestions.questionText: Using the given scale, calculate the distance as the crow flies from Johannesburg to Kimberley. (On the map the route measures about 4 cm and the bar scale is about 3,1 cm to 300 km.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Distance = (4 ÷ 3,1) × 300 km = 425,8 km
(Various reasonable measurements of the line and bar scale are accepted.)

Mark 1: measuring the straight-line distance on the map
Mark 2: using the bar scale
Mark 3: answer ≈ 425,8 km

subQuestions.label: 4.2.4 (iv)
subQuestions.questionText: The delivery truck travels the 505,5 km from Johannesburg to Kimberley at a speed of 98 km/h. Determine the time the truck will arrive in Kimberley if it left Johannesburg at 09:00. Give your answer to the nearest minute in the format hh:mm.
subQuestions.memoText:
Time = 505,5 ÷ 98 = 5,15816 hours
0,15816 × 60 ≈ 9 minutes
= 5 hours 9 minutes
09:00 + 5:09 = 14:09

Mark 1: 505,5 ÷ 98
Mark 2: 5,158 hours
Mark 3: 5 hours 9 minutes
Mark 4: 09:00 + 5:09 = 14:09

subQuestions.label: 4.2.4 (v)
subQuestions.questionText: On the return journey, the truck takes 3 hours 20 minutes to complete the 505,5 km trip. Determine the speed of the return journey.
subQuestions.memoText:
3 hours 20 minutes = 3⅓ hours = 3,333 hours
Speed = 505,5 ÷ 3,333 = 151,65 km/h

Mark 1: converting 3 h 20 min to hours
Mark 2: 505,5 ÷ 3,333 → 151,65 km/h

questions.title: Stellenbosch University — Street Map, Floor Plan, Scale, Carpet Cleaning and Paint

subQuestions.questionText: Use the map of Stellenbosch University. The Engineering Faculty lies on the corner of which two streets?
subQuestions.memoText:
Banghoek Street and Joubert Street (accept Hammanshand Street and Joubert Street).

[Award 2 marks — 1 per street]

subQuestions.questionText: Sofi googled directions to a specific street: 'Travel in a Southerly direction along Joubert Street, turning left into Merriman Road. Follow the road to the traffic circle, taking the third turn, left off the circle.' Name the street Sofi was looking for.
subQuestions.memoText:
Marais Street

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Study the floor plan of Sofi's flat (dimensions in metres). Determine the length and width of the flat excluding the patio.
subQuestions.memoText:
Length = 5,8 m
Width = 4,5 m

Mark 1: length 5,8 m
Mark 2: width 4,5 m

subQuestions.questionText: State how many windows are found on the Southern side of the flat.
subQuestions.memoText:
2 windows

[Award 2 marks for reading the floor plan]

subQuestions.questionText: By measuring the length of Line A (which represents 4,5 m and measures about 8 cm on the plan), determine the unit scale of the floor plan.
subQuestions.memoText:
4,5 m = 450 cm
450 cm ÷ 8 cm = 56,25
Unit scale = 1 : 56,25 (accept 1 : 56)

Mark 1: converting 4,5 m to 450 cm
Mark 2: ÷ 8 → 1 : 56,25

subQuestions.questionText: Sofi needs to clean the carpet in her 3 m by 3 m bedroom. The advert reads: 'Fitted Carpets (less than 5 sq metres) R750,00. PLUS 5 to 20 sq metres R145,00/m². Minimum fee includes cleaning of up to R750,00.' Show, with calculations, whether Sofi can afford to have her bedroom cleaned with her budget of R1 000.
subQuestions.memoText:
Area of room = 3 × 3 = 9 m²
First 5 m² = R750,00
Remaining area = 9 − 5 = 4 m² at R145,00/m² = R580,00
Total cost = R750 + R580 = R1 330
R1 330 > R1 000, so Sofi cannot afford to have her bedroom cleaned.

Mark 1: area = 9 m²
Mark 2: first 5 m² = R750
Mark 3: 9 − 5 = 4 m²
Mark 4: 4 × R145
Mark 5: total R1 330
Mark 6: conclusion — she cannot afford it

subQuestions.questionText: Sofi wants to paint the wall behind her bed. The wall is 3 m long and 1,8 m high. Two coats of paint are required, and one litre of paint covers 6 m². Determine how much paint is needed to paint this wall.
subQuestions.memoText:
Area of wall = 3 × 1,8 = 5,4 m²
For two coats: 5,4 × 2 = 10,8 m²
Paint needed = 10,8 ÷ 6 = 1,8 litres

Mark 1: 3 × 1,8
Mark 2: area = 5,4 m²
Mark 3: × 2 (two coats)
Mark 4: 10,8 m²
Mark 5: ÷ 6 → 1,8 litres

subQuestions.questionText: Using the scale 1 : 50, describe the scaled rectangle you would draw to represent the back wall of the bedroom (3 m by 1,8 m).
subQuestions.memoText:
3 m = 300 cm → 300 ÷ 50 = 6 cm
1,8 m = 180 cm → 180 ÷ 50 = 3,6 cm
Draw a rectangle 6 cm by 3,6 cm.

Mark 1: 300 ÷ 50 = 6 cm
Mark 2: 180 ÷ 50 = 3,6 cm

subQuestions.questionText: Sofi will place a double bed (140 cm wide) and two bedside tables (61 cm wide each) against the back wall of the bedroom (3 m long), exactly against the centre of the wall. Calculate (in cm) how much wall length is left over on either side of the bed and side tables.
subQuestions.memoText:
Back wall = 3 m = 300 cm
Space used = 140 cm + (61 cm × 2) = 140 + 122 = 262 cm
Left over = 300 − 262 = 38 cm
On either side = 38 ÷ 2 = 19 cm

Mark 1: converting 3 m to 300 cm
Mark 2: 61 × 2 = 122 cm
Mark 3: 140 + 122 = 262 cm
Mark 4: 300 − 262 = 38 cm
Mark 5: ÷ 2 → 19 cm on either side
